Input variablePhysical meaningSI dimensions
Raarithmetic_mean_absolute_height (Ra)
First-order absolute moment of surface height fluctuations (mean absolute deviation of height), a measure of average roughness height.
L
ktpeak_to_valley_height (kt)
Peak-to-valley height (difference between highest peak and lowest valley) of the surface topography.
L
k_rmsroot_mean_square_height (k_rms)
Root-mean-square height of surface fluctuations (standard deviation of height), a measure of roughness amplitude.
L
Skskewness_of_height_fluctuations (Sk)
Skewness of the roughness height distribution (third standardized moment), describes asymmetry of height fluctuations.
1 (dimensionless)
Kukurtosis_of_height_fluctuations (Ku)
Kurtosis of the roughness height distribution (fourth standardized moment), describes peakedness/tail weight of height fluctuations.
1 (dimensionless)
ESeffective_streamwise_slope (ES)
Effective streamwise slope of the roughness (dimensionless gradient measure of surface asperities in the flow direction).
1 (dimensionless)
Posurface_porosity (Po)
Surface porosity (fraction of surface area occupied by voids), a dimensionless fraction between 0 and 1.
1 (dimensionless)
? denotes an unspecified SI exponent.

Per-variable physical reasoning and program checks

Ra

The typed candidate labels Ra as the arithmetic mean absolute height (first-order absolute moment). The KB record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness has canonical_quantity 'arithmetic mean roughness' with symbols Ra, R_a and the definition 'Mean absolute deviation of surface height...' which is exactly the quantity named in the ledger; its si_dimension is L (length), so it justifies the single nonzero L exponent. The additional KB record pq_mean_roughness_height documents an area-averaged surface height (another mean-height measure) and also has si_dimension L, supporting that Ra is a length-based roughness statistic in the original roughness parameterization. These records directly apply to the Ra in the problem (matching symbol and definition) and support the proposed SI exponents.

kt

The ledger defines kt as the 'peak-to-valley height' of surface topography. The KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height lists symbols including kt and the definition 'A roughness-amplitude measure formed from vertical height differences between peaks and valleys.' Its si_dimension is L (length). The record therefore applies directly to the ledger's kt (same symbol and definition) and justifies the single nonzero L exponent in the candidate vector.

k_rms

The ledger defines k_rms as the root-mean-square height of surface fluctuations. The KB record pq_rms_roughness_height has canonical_quantity 'root-mean-square roughness height' with symbols k_rms and the definition 'Root-mean-square fluctuation of surface height about its mean.' It records si_dimension L, matching the ledger meaning and supporting the proposed L-only exponent vector for k_rms.

Sk

The ledger names Sk as the skewness of roughness height fluctuations (third standardized moment). The KB record pq_height_skewness defines 'surface-height skewness' with symbols Sk and states explicitly that it is a 'Third standardized moment' and 'si_dimension: 1' (dimensionless). This record matches the ledger symbol and definition and therefore justifies the candidate zero exponents (dimensionless) for Sk.

Ku

The ledger defines Ku as kurtosis of height fluctuations (fourth standardized moment). The KB record pq_height_kurtosis lists canonical_quantity 'surface-height kurtosis', symbols Ku, and description 'Fourth standardized moment' with si_dimension 1 (dimensionless). The symbol and definition match the ledger variable, supporting the candidate dimensionless exponent vector for Ku.

ES

The ledger describes ES as the effective streamwise slope of the roughness (a gradient measure). The KB record pq_effective_surface_slope defines 'effective surface slope' with symbols ES and notes 'Mean absolute gradient of surface height in a specified horizontal direction' and explicitly states that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and is therefore dimensionless (si_dimension 1). The record directly corresponds to the ledger ES and supports the all-zero SI exponent vector.

Po

The ledger defines Po as surface porosity (fraction of surface area occupied by voids). The KB record pq_porosity lists symbols Po and defines porosity as a 'Fraction of void or open volume/area' with si_dimension 1 (dimensionless). The record matches the ledger variable's symbol and physical meaning and justifies the candidate dimensionless exponent vector for Po.

Reproduce

Install the dependencies from the repository root.

python -m pip install -e ".[app,notebooks]"

To generate these cards from the included result, run the first part of the case notebook. It reads the selected run and displays its cards and figures.

To repeat the analysis using the case data and settings, configure the model services described in the environment settings, then run:

ai-buckingham sandgrain

Open result.html in the new directory under generated/cases/sandgrain/. The notebook's final section also runs the analysis and displays its new report.
